headline: Stated no concerns with Section 106 review of proposed antenna project at 31 East Spring Street.
summary: Members reviewed a proposed antenna project at 31 East Spring Street under Section 106 review. They voted unanimously to state no concerns with the project. Members also heard updates on the Armory project and the Comprehensive Plan, and discussed proposed federal changes to Section 106.
decisions: Approved the August 12, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Stated no concerns with the proposed antenna project at 31 East Spring Street, unanimously.

decision_titles: Section 106 review for 31 East Spring Street antenna project
plain_text:
9/9/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Britta Tonn, Chair; Doug Johnson; Sue O’Brien; Maggie Hicks
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning
Guests Present:
Call to Order by: Britta
Meeting Start Time: 6:04 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi 
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by Sue, seconded by Doug, to approve the August 12, 2026 meeting minutes.
Discussion: Doug suggested a minor change on the first page.
Voting unanimous. Motion carried.
Section 106 Review: 31 East Spring Street
Ravi gave an overview of the proposed project and the purpose of Section 106 Review. Britta 
gave background on the role of Section 106 review for telecommunication projects. Britta and 
Doug noted that the proposed antenna would be minimally visible because of its location on the 
building and the surrounding vegetation. Doug and Sue said given that the existing antenna at a 
similar height, the visual impact would be minimal. Ravi and the board discussed the ground-
level structures, and the proposed screening.
Motion by Doug, seconded by Sue, to state that the board has no concerns with the proposed 
project at 31 East Spring ST. Voting: unanimous. Motion carried.
City Updates
Ravi said that the Armory project is on the Development Review Board’s meeting agenda for 
next week. Ravi gave an update on the status of the Comprehensive Plan.
Other Business
Britta overviewed the proposed changes to Section 106 at the federal level that would remove 
Certified Local Governments as a consulting party for projects. Britta said that this would deeply 
negatively impact historic preservation in the United States. Britta posted the following links in 
the chat for more information:
l https://culturalheritagepartners.com/war-room-for-threats-to-section-106/
l https://www.vermontpublic.org/show/vermont-edition/2026-08-26/how-proposed-
federal-changes-could-impact-vermonts-historic-sites
Adjourn
Motion by: Doug
Second: Britta
Meeting End Time: 6:45 pm
I.
